reviews.review: If you have a couple of friends to play this with, it's definitely worth buying. Right now, we love playing this game from time to time, even though there is not much of an endgame yet (the gameplay is just so fun that we keep playing). When the developers release more endgame content, it's going to be one hell of a game

Considering the great start this game had way back in 2020 and the Seasons leading up to Season 03, it's a wonder to see just how badly GSG have fumbled the bag time and time again with the subsequent Seasonal updates after Season 03: Plaguefall.

Season 04 was the one that made me put DRG down simply because of how absolutely stupid broken the Stingtail was (and still kind of is, despite the changes) and picking the game up again in 2026 I've noticed a theme of every update introducing some kind of enemy that simple was NOT required to be in the game in the first place, such as the Corespawn Crawlers of Season 05 or the [i] god-forsaken [/i] Ossiran Scrab, which is an even more annoying Jellyfish but is armored and constantly gets in your face if you're any other class than Driller to deal with them.

Let's also not forget that there are some serious long-standing bugs that have been in the game for over HALF A DECADE now that haven't been fixed or even really acknowledged by GSG - the main big one to me being the bug that gets players stuck inside of the On-Site Refining mission's pipelines. It's something that got reported 6 years ago and still happens to players on that mission to this day, almost always requiring a full mission restart.

Deep Rock Galactic is one of my favorite games on Steam. It's absolutely bursting with personality and tremendously fun to play, but then it leaves behind that infuriating desire to squeeze more game out of it. Let me explain.

DRG is a 4-player co-operative game where players are dropped into a mine of some pre-determined complexity and length, to accomplish some objective. Each player chooses a dwarf from a roster of four, each a unique class: Gunner, Driller, Engineer, and Scout. Each dwarf has a different loadout with different weapons and tools. Multiple players can use the same dwarf unless the host says otherwise. The players, upon entering the mine, have to bore through swarms of enemy bugs whilst working together to navigate the caves and secure various resources on the way to completing the aforementioned objective. Once the objective is completed, the players must then navigate to a drop pod for extraction.

Regarding the dwarves. The player will likely pick one or two dwarves that they like and search out opportunities to play them. Each dwarf has unique weapons and tools, and is designed in such a way that missing one feels like a disadvantage. The Gunner has a Minigun to grant him great firepower, a deployable shield that repels enemies and recharges shields, and a zip-line for crossing large lateral distances. The Driller has a flamethrower that devastates enemies at close range, a satchel charge which devastates allies at close range, and a set of power drills capable of tunneling toward objectives. The engineer has two deployable turrets and an extremely nifty, never to be underestimated platform gun. The scout has an incredibly handy grappling hook and a very helpful flare gun. 

The game is fun to play. It takes awhile to experience everything it has to offer, and even then it can still shuffle things around to surprise you. The variety of enemies and biomes combine to make interesting and challenging instances. One game might have the player traversing narrow corridors looking for veins of ore while in another one they're searching a humongous cavern for alien eggs. In one, they're running from cavern to cavern fighting bugs that come rolling across the sand while in another they're fighting swarms of flying enemies in caustic caverns, desperately trying to avoid being carried off. 

The game oozes personality. There is so much to enjoy about the world that DRG portrays. The dwarves are miners who love their job, hate their job, and love to hate their job. The first five minutes of gameplay are spent figuring out how many ways you can piss off that kill-joy from Mission Control. Every game begins and ends with dwarves shouting a myriad of "Rock and Stone!" and "For Karl!" Shooting allies by accident has them calling out, "Stop shooting me, you pointy eared leaf-lover!" In between missions, it's customary to have a drink at the Abyss Bar, or six, and chuck the empty mugs at companions. But in the mine, it's all business, with everyone rushing to do their part mining or killing enemies so that they look good on the ending scoreboard. 

DRG has a lot going for it- plenty to provide tens of hours of entertainment at least. The one biggest problem the game has is that it takes a fairly small amount of time to unlock all of the customizations and loadout upgrades, and many of them are completely passable. Eventually, the player will not have any specific drive, objective, or goal, and will play the game just for the sake of playing the game. The desire to progress and distinguish oneself doesn't quite feel satisfied with what's available currently. It's the best problem to have, because it implies that the game has much more room to grow.

A note on connecting with other players: The system works really well. In Co-op games, people will undoubtedly worry whether or not it's important to have friends who play the game. While having friends to play with is always beneficial, the multiplayer system in this game is such that it is easy to find people to play with. On a personal note, I've very rarely had trouble with strangers in the game. One or two times I've been kicked to make room in a group for a host's friend or some other nonsense, but 98% of the time a game will just proceed normally with the only interactions being marking targets and chanting "Rock and Stone!" and I wouldn't have it any other way. The game does support voice chat, and I've heard people talking, but I prefer to use the text box.

A few anecdotes:
Three dwarves chanting "Rock and Stone!" from the safety of a drop pod while a fourth comes sprinting up. As the gate closes on him, out of the cacophony comes a "Leave no dwarf behind!"

A scout emerges from a blizzard to assist a downed dwarf in a wide icy cavern, dozens of bugs swarm after him. He gets the dwarf to his feet and quickly shoots onward as the swarm overtakes him, off to pick up the next dwarf in the circle.

One dwarf approaches another who had ventured off from the group and gotten himself downed, but before he can pick the dwarf up a long tentacle latches onto his head and carries him, screaming, up to the ceiling.

A scout tries to outpace a swarm enough to rescue a driller. As the driller finds his feet, he panic throws a satchel charge and instantly detonates it, sending a bewildered scout in a heap across the cavern.

A group of four dwarves are running for a drop pod, chased by a half-dozen winged bugs with only seconds to spare. As the fourth one approaches, the three already inside watch from what they believe to be safety- but as he climbs the ramp, one of the flying bugs latches itself onto one of the dwarves inside and carries him off. The others shoot at it but no one leaves the pod before the gate slams shut.

Rock and Stone!
